text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging: p99 latency spike detected for canary deployment 'redwood-canary-v7' in eu-west-1. Metric: inference-p99 = 2.4s (baseline 300ms). Alert threshold breached at 1915012345.

Maya (oncall): saw it. getting eyes. is this a traffic shift or a model issue?

Jonas (eng-runtime): looks correlated with the v7 rollout that started ~1915012300 — traffic ramped to 20% via the canary. I see increased tail latency on streaming paths (server->client stalls).

Priya (eng-sre): linking dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/inference-canary?orgId=1&var-env=prod

Sam (infra): infra checks: GPU utilization normal, no node OOMs. autoscaler didn't trigger.

Jonas (eng-runtime): pulling logs from the canary:
```
2026-03-14T09:45:01Z canary-inference request_id=aa12 latency=12ms
2026-03-14T09:45:04Z canary-inference request_id=aa13 latency=2400ms stream-stalled at token 87
2026-03-14T09:45:04Z canary-inference request_id=aa14 kv-cache-miss
2026-03-14T09:45:06Z canary-inference request_id=aa15 latency=2600ms tail
```

Jonas (eng-runtime): pattern: KV-cache misses + streaming stalls. v7 changed attention kernel ordering and has a slightly different prefix handling; may be causing more cache fragmentation.

Maya (oncall): customer impact? any 5xxs?

Linh (cust-succ): I already flagged to a pilot customer on v7 traffic (acme-inc). They reported timeouts in their streaming UI ~09:45. No user-facing 500s, mostly client-side timeouts and degraded UX.

Priya (eng-sre): rolling alert noise: p95 rose from 150ms -> 380ms, p99 -> 2.4s. Error budget burn increasing. Paging primary oncall. Recommend immediate mitigation: reduce canary traffic, enable fallback to v6 for streaming calls, or rollback.

Jonas (eng-runtime): quick mitigation options:
- Option A: traffic-shift rollback v7 -> v6 (instant routing change)
- Option B: reduce v7 weight to 0.5% (gradual)
- Option C: enable model-variant fallback for streaming (forces alternate path)

deploy-bot: Rollout event: v7 promoted to canary at 1915012200 -> weight 20%.

Maya (oncall): I will reduce traffic to 1% now and watch. initiating via routing tool.

Maya (oncall): /run set-canary-weight redwood-canary-v7 1%

deploy-bot: Command accepted. Canaries API: set weight redwood-canary-v7 -> 1% (user=Maya).

Jonas (eng-runtime): good. also flipping streaming fallback for canary: /ops enable-fallback streaming redwood-canary-v7 -> uses v6 streaming path if stall detected.

Priya (eng-sre): do we need a rollback? if p99 doesn't drop within 3 minutes, recommend rollback.

Sam (infra): I'm scaling up the canary pool by +1 instance (g4x) to see if stalls are node-specific.

Maya (oncall): status update in 90s.

(90s later)

Maya (oncall): after weight drop to 1% and fallback enabled: p95 = 170ms, p99 = 380ms, streaming stall counts decreased from 18/min -> 2/min. KPIs improving.

Jonas (eng-runtime): logs show stall signatures reduced. The kv-cache miss rate is still slightly elevated on v7 instances — looks like quantization layout changed cache keys (hash salt mismatch possible). Will run a deeper check but immediate mitigation looks effective.

Priya (eng-sre): incident classification: Sev3 for now due to partial customer impact (pilot customers) and SLO burn. No broad outage.

Linh (cust-succ): letting acme-inc know we throttled canary traffic and enabled fallback — they'll retest and report back.

Maya (oncall): next steps: Jonas to triage model-level cache/mismatch; if root cause confirmed, schedule a rollback and gate v7 for rework. If not reproducible, we can slowly re-increase weight with tighter monitoring. Sam to monitor infra for any residual anomalies. Priya to create post-incident slack thread for RCAs and add an eval prompt set to compare v6/v7 streaming token emission.

Jonas (eng-runtime): quick grep found a change in v7 startup that appends a model-version salt to cache key for experimental deduping. That could explain mismatch for hot prefixes:
```
// v6 cache key
key = prefix_hash + seq_len
// v7 cache key
key = prefix_hash + seq_len + model_version_salt
```
If different workers disagree about the salt (race on config), you'll get misses and recomputation leading to stalls.

Sam (infra): checking rollout infra: config propagation lag was ~20s around rollout time due to control-plane batching. if salt depends on config push, some nodes may have old salt.

Maya (oncall): agree. sounds like a config-atomicity problem. For now we'll keep v7 at 1% and run a controlled test: spin a private v7 pool with config-propagation fixes.

Priya (eng-sre): I'll open the incident ticket: INC-2026-0314-17 with timeline, mitigations, and assigned owners.

Linh (cust-succ): acme-inc acknowledged the mitigation and confirmed streaming is back to normal on their end. :+1:

Maya (oncall): handoff: I'm handing to Jonas for ongoing debug. Oncall shift ends in 30m. If p99 creeps >1.5s again, page the oncall escalation.

Jonas (eng-runtime): taking it. I'll freeze any further canary ramps until we have config-atomicity fix and a patch to unify cache salt generation.

Priya (eng-sre): adding runbook notes:
- If canary-induced tail spikes: 1) immediately reduce weight to <=1% 2) enable fallback 3) consider rollback if no improvement in 3 min 4) check config propagation logs and kv-cache miss rate 5) notify customers in pilot.

Maya (oncall): thanks team. closing live mitigation phase, keeping thread open for RCA.

Jonas (eng-runtime): will post a follow-up test plan and root-cause analysis later today.

deploy-bot: Action log: canary weight set -> 1% by Maya at 1915012365; fallback toggled by Jonas at 1915012380; infra scale +1 by Sam at 1915012390.

Priya (eng-sre): incident status -> mitigated (SLO degradation contained). Ticket INC-2026-0314-17 created.

Maya (oncall): handoff complete.
